reference_sql:
SELECT product_id, week_start, units,
  ROUND(AVG(units) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY week_start ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS avg_units_4w,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY week_start ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS weeks_in_window
FROM weekly_units
WHERE product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 20
  AND week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-06' AND DATE '2025-06-23'
alternatives:
WITH wk AS (
  -- one row per product and week in the range
  SELECT product_id, week_start, units
  FROM weekly_units
  WHERE product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 20
    AND week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-06' AND DATE '2025-06-23'
)
SELECT w.product_id, w.week_start, w.units, ROUND(AVG(p.units), 2) AS avg_units_4w, COUNT(*) AS weeks_in_window
FROM wk w
JOIN wk p ON p.product_id = w.product_id AND p.week_start BETWEEN w.week_start - INTERVAL 21 DAY AND w.week_start
GROUP BY w.product_id, w.week_start, w.units

WITH m AS (
  -- one row per product and week in the range
  SELECT product_id, week_start, units,
    AVG(units) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY week_start ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_4w,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY week_start ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS n
  FROM weekly_units
  WHERE product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 20
    AND week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-06' AND DATE '2025-06-23'
)
SELECT product_id, week_start, units, ROUND(avg_4w, 2) AS avg_units_4w, n AS weeks_in_window
FROM m

other_way.tradeoff: A self-join on the 3 weeks before gives the same averages because every week has a row, but it is longer than one frame.
